text.p: Canadian 88 Energy Corp, on the heels of a failed takover bid for Morrison Petroleums Ltd, said on Monday it set its 1997 capital spending budget at a record C$110 million.
Canadian 88 said most of the funds would be spent in Alberta along the foothills region, with a minimum of C$50 million to be spent on its Olds/Crossfield properties.
Olds/Crossfield activity would include 24 deep horizontal gas wells targeting the Devonian formation, as well as expenditures on its Olds gas plant and gathering system, it said.

Canadian 88 also said 1997 spending, which is 34.1 percent higher than that in 1996, would include at least C$30 million developing its Waterton natural gas discovery in southwest Alberta, where a multi-well development drilling program was planned.
The play was expected to add over 100 million cubic feet per day to Canadian 88's gas output over the next 12 months, it said.
Canadian 88, under fire from securities regulators, scrapped a C$652 million hostile bid for Morrison in early February.
Morrison later struck a merger deal with Northstar Energy Corp, which said on Monday nearly all Morrison shares had been tendered to its stock-swap proposal.
